key_insight: AlphaTensor-Quantum can be reused without retraining to optimize T-count across a broad range of quantum circuits, achieving larger T-count reductions and demonstrating generalizable, efficient circuit optimization.
problem_solved: High T-counts in quantum circuits drive up error-correction overhead and resource costs; many ML-based optimizers require retraining for new circuit families. This work removes the need for retraining while delivering substantial T-count savings across diverse circuits.
method: Reuse and extend the pre-trained AlphaTensor-Quantum model as a transfer/zero-shot optimizer to tackle new circuit families without retraining.
Apply model-guided decomposition and rewrite strategies to identify T-gate–efficient circuit transformations and rewrite sequences.
Systematic benchmarking across diverse circuit types to quantify T-count reductions and validate generalizability and efficiency.
impact: Reducing T-counts without retraining lowers fault-tolerant resource requirements and accelerates deployment of quantum algorithms; practitioners can integrate pre-trained AI models into compilation flows to get immediate gains without costly retraining.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: AlphaTensor-Quantum reused → model-guided rewrites → optimized circuit (emphasize 'no retraining')
Bar chart: comparative T-count reduction across different circuit families (before vs after)
Heatmap or scatter: improvement magnitude vs circuit type/size to show generalizability
Icon set: T-gate cost reduction, clock/effort saved (no retraining), and hardware/resource impact
paper_title: Reusability report: Optimizing T count in general quantum circuits with AlphaTensor-Quantum
paper_authors: Remmy Zen, Maximilian Nägele, Florian Marquardt
